images.title: A triangle is half its rectangle
images.purpose: Show the triangle inside its outer rectangle so that half of base times height is visible.
images.composition: One triangle drawn inside its outer rectangle, the altitude dashed, two short calculations underneath.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, the main figure large and centred with generous empty margins on all sides, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills, nothing else in the frame. A rectangle 8 units wide and 5 units tall drawn with a thin #6B7280 outline and very light grey fill. Inside it a triangle whose base is the whole bottom edge of the rectangle and whose top vertex touches the top edge 3 units from the left corner; the triangle is filled #0072B2. A dashed #CC79A7 altitude runs straight down from the top vertex to the base, with a small right angle mark at its foot. Label '8 cm' under the base and '5 cm' beside the dashed altitude. Below the figure, two lines of text, left aligned: 'Rectangle: 8 × 5 = 40 cm²' and 'Triangle: 1/2 × 8 × 5 = 20 cm²'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The triangle is exactly half its outer rectangle, so its area is 1/2 × base × height.
images.description: Show the triangle inside its outer rectangle so that half of base times height is visible.
images.context: Concept T3.C2; one image showing only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: The two grey side regions each mirror a part of the triangle, which is why it is exactly half.

image_decisions.why: The half in the formula is only convincing when the outer rectangle is seen around the triangle.
